neighbours.label: a prohibitive or normative negation telling someone what not to do or what should not happen ('don't dismiss', 'should not be blamed'), as against factual or narrative negation
fire: It's tempting, but don't ignore the warning lights on your dashboard.
Those nurses deserve our thanks and should not be blamed for the shortages.
Whatever happens at the interview, don't underestimate how nervous they are.
Refugees fleeing war ought to be welcomed, not demonised.
If your child is upset, don't brush off their worries as silly.
Young players make mistakes, and they shouldn't be punished for every one.
I understand your anger, but please don't take it out on the staff.
Volunteers should be supported and not criticised for trying to help.
quiet: It was dark, and he didn't notice the warning lights on his dashboard.
Those nurses worked double shifts because the hospital was short of staff.
At the interview last week, she didn't seem nervous at all.
The refugees did not reach the border until late on Sunday night.
When my child was upset, she didn't tell anyone about her worries.
The young players did not score in the first half of the match.
The manager wasn't in the office, so we spoke to the staff instead.
The volunteers did not arrive until the food had already been served.

predictions: fire 0.3-0.55 on n't/not or the verb after it in advice; narrative 'didn't', factual 'did not' 0.0-0.06
